Core Classes¶

This module defines the core classes behind the algorithms. These will often not be used directly, but are used under the hood.

Mat¶

This class handles all matrix like objects at the top level. It defines the basic properties and is used as the foundation of all lower matrix classes.

class stoch_imp.core_classes.Mat(arr, *args, **kwargs)[source]¶

Top level class for all matrix-like objects such as Vectors, WMatrix, EqMatrix, etc.

Variables:

  • mat – The internal sympy.Matrix representation of the object.

  • dim – Number of rows in the matrix (system size).

  • iter – Iterator over all (row, column) index pairs in the matrix.

  • zero_index – Boolean indicating whether 0-based indexing is used.

  • is_symbolic – Boolean indicating whether the matrix is treated as symbolic.

  • tol – Numerical tolerance used for approximate comparisons.

In-place symbolic simplification of the matrix.

Return type:

None

TrMatrix¶

This class handles all transition matrices, and safeguards the mathematical properties. A transition matrix is a matrix \(W\) whose off diagonal elements are non-negative, and whose diagonal elements are given by \(- \sum_{i: i \neq j} W_{ij}\), such that the columns sum to zero.

class stoch_imp.core_classes.TrMatrix(arr, *args, **kwargs)[source]¶

Class handling all transition matrices. These matrices should sum to zero along columns and have positive off-diagonal elements.

Variables:

  • mat – Internal sympy.Matrix representation.

  • dim – Number of rows in the matrix.

  • iter – Iterator over matrix indices.

  • zero_index – Boolean indicating whether 0-based indexing is used.

  • is_symbolic – Boolean indicating whether the matrix is in symbolic form.

  • tol – Numerical tolerance used for validations.

Parameters:

arr (Any)

add_trans(i, j, r=1.0, ri=None, symm=True, simp=True)[source]¶

Add a transition i –> j with rate r, and optionally symmetric transition j –> i with rate ri.

Parameters:

  • i (int) – Start index

  • j (int) – Target index

  • r (float | Expr) – Transition rate from i to j

  • ri (float | Expr | None) – Optional inverse rate (j to i)

  • symm (bool) – If True, adds j –> i with rate 1/r or ri

  • simp (bool) – If True, simplifies r and ri

Return type:

None

CoeffArray¶

This class is a custom class for 3D arrays used to store the \(A^{(k)}_{mn}\) coefficients and simplify retrieval when calculating conductances.

class stoch_imp.core_classes.CoeffArray(n)[source]¶

(n, n, n) dim coefficient array class for storing transition coefficients. Prints pretty.

Variables:

  • mat – The array of coefficients

  • iter – A simple iterator to iterate over the whole array. Use as (elem in self.iter) or (i, j, k in self.iter)

Parameters:

n (int)

to_num()[source]¶

Convert array to numeric type

Return type:

None

to_sym()[source]¶

Convert array to symbolic type

Return type:

None

It forwards all indexing to numpy, and cn be used as a numpy array. The main reason for its existence is that it prints any symbolic expressions pretty.

ConstantObject¶

This is a mixin class used for explicitly constant objects, objects that do not contain any driving. It allows the definition of a numeric matrix which is impossible for driven objects, as they would lose their dependence on the driving symbol.

class stoch_imp.core_classes.ConstantObject(nmat, *args, **kwargs)[source]¶

Stores the numeric matrix form of a symbolic matrix when symbolic evaluation is disabled.

Variables:

nmat – Numeric matrix representation if symbolic flag is False; otherwise None.

ConstantMatrix¶

This class is the most general class for constant matrices. Most constant objects that are not an EqMatrix will be of this type

class stoch_imp.core_classes.ConstantMatrix(*args, **kwargs)[source]¶

Matrix class that supports both symbolic and numeric representations, with conversion between the two.

Inherits from ConstantObject and Mat to combine symbolic matrix functionality with numeric handling.

Variables:

  • mat – Internal sympy.Matrix representation.

  • nmat – Numeric matrix representation (if symbolic mode is off).

  • dim – Number of rows in the matrix.

  • iter – Iterator over matrix indices.

  • zero_index – Boolean indicating whether 0-based indexing is used.

  • is_symbolic – Boolean indicating whether the matrix is in symbolic form.

  • tol – Numerical tolerance used for operations.
